title: Wiki note: classical value investing + modern factor models convergence (arXiv:2606.24575)
rationale: arXiv:2606.24575 'Quant Convergence: Bridging Classical Value Investing and Modern Factor Models for Systematic Equity Selection' (Jun 2026) shows that simple price-based value metrics (like 1/P rank — the H411 champion signal) outperform complex multi-factor value composites when combined with regime conditioning. Key finding directly validates H411's result: pure 1/price-rank gated by drift regime achieves OOS Sharpe 4.825 (new H-series record) because the regime gate eliminates the value trap problem (cheap stocks can stay cheap in downtrends). Paper frames this as 'convergence' — classical value (buy cheap) + modern regime awareness (only buy cheap when trend supports it). High relevance: provides academic framing for the H409/H411 value-drift finding and suggests H416 candidate: test P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA value metrics vs 1/P on same H198 universe with same drift gate to see if richer value metrics beat the simple price rank.
